evidence.summary: Round 3 (Warren decision 2026-10-08) measured on cip READ ONLY for the round 3 worker (started 14:49:56): five full regular runs stored 3.68, 6.47, 6.37, 0.77 and 5.87 MB of snapshots (avg 4.63 MB, 25-51 of 175-176 rows kept) vs 17.3-18.5 MB per run on the round 2 worker the same afternoon (all 176 kept) and ~20 MB in round 1: about 74% less, ~0.22 GB/day instead of ~0.95. Payload-less rows average 624 B (~5 MB/day). Snapshot payload is capped by the daily 90-day retention (cip_test + unit tested; never deletes rows), so it stops growing at about 20 GB at the measured rate; rows (kept forever by decision) grow ~1.9 GB/year. No paid service or new dependency.

rationale: Pass because payload growth is now bounded exactly as decided (on-change/failure storage + 90-day payload retention) and rows-forever is Warren's call. Limits: retention has not run on cip or in the worker yet (nothing is over 90 days until about 2026-11-07; first beat run 03:15 2026-10-09 should clear 0); the 20 GB ceiling is an estimate from five runs, not a multi-day measurement; Amazon failed-parse (CAPTCHA) pages are ~95% of what remains and are kept because the decision stores every failed parse (cut needs open item 2 / N-0085 decision 1); two Evetech 404 listings (120, 121) are stored every run (~5 MB/day) because their 404 page parses ok (deferred finding); Postgres reuses cleared space only after vacuum, file does not shrink.
